column1: # cyanrip-fork release ledger — APPEND ONLY.
# Publication is an ACT, not a derivable fact: no amount of reading this tree
# tells you that a build was handed to somebody. So this file is the one input
# to the release manifest that a human writes, and everything else in
# release-manifest.json is derived from it plus the record plus git.
# RULES, enforced by tools/gen-release-manifest.py and pinned by tests:
#   * seq increments by one per published artifact, stable or beta alike.
#   * seq is NEVER reused and NEVER reset, including across a version-scheme
#     change or an upstream sync. It is the only orderable thing we publish --
#     our version string is not orderable at all, because the part that
#     advances is SemVer build metadata, which the spec ignores for precedence.
#   * A row is never edited or deleted once written. A mistake is corrected by
#     appending a new row, exactly like a handshake lap.
#   * `commit` is the commit that was PUBLISHED, which is not the commit that
#     set the version. Those differ whenever the derived artifacts are
#     regenerated after the bump -- see CLAUDE.md, "choose the released commit
#     after the artifacts agree".
# On the historical rows: seq 1-11 record the commit that SET each version,
# because that is what is recoverable from this tree today (git log -S over
# meson.build). Only seq 12 records a commit verified to pass its own suite at
# that commit. Said plainly rather than implied, because a column that means
# two different things in different rows is the defect this project keeps
# finding. Historical betas are superseded and are not installable targets;
# they are here so the sequence is complete and monotonic.
# seq
